gate_reasoning: Stage 4 produces 47 scored claims with 43% scoring Low — above the target ceiling of 30% Low for a clean ship-as-is decision and above the internal quality bar of 10–20% Low. The high Low rate is driven by three structural patterns: (1) heavy reliance on vendor-authored content from RTTVP vendors (FourKites, Shippeo, project44, Beacon, TransmetriQ) for the core operating-cost and frequency statistics in Pain points 4.1 and 4.2; (2) exclusive use of auto-Low aggregators (Mordor, Grand View, MarkNtel, ZoomInfo, Future Market Insights) for market sizing; and (3) chain-of-citations failures where Gartner and MIT statistics are cited only through vendor blogs. The nine High-confidence claims are well-sourced (McKinsey 95/42 tier visibility, E2open 10-K, Descartes 40-F, K+N annual report, Maersk annual report, ASEAN Single Window, NTT DATA 2024 study, Gartner May 2025 prediction, ASEAN pain-point 4.5 government data) and the structural narrative is coherent. Before shipping to a client, three deep-research actions are required: (A) cross-validate the Beacon.com 13.9% ETA accuracy figure with Sea-Intelligence or BIMCO schedule reliability data; (B) source the 62% industry RTTVP tracking rate independently from a non-vendor source; (C) either find a primary citation for the Gartner 34-manual-updates figure or remove it. Eight ASSUMED-N claims are appropriately tagged and represent genuine data gaps rather than sourcing failures.
